_source: Each state's (and D.C.'s) own election authority: the page on its own domain, or a vendor portal it links as its official tool, for each voting task. Registration-status, polling-place and absentee pages as NASS's Can I Vote (nass.org/can-i-vote, the Secretaries of State's own directory) lists them, each opened and stored where it lands; a dead one replaced from the authority's own site. Never a third-party aggregator as a destination. The register task is not here: it is election_calendar.json's `register` (one copy of each URL), checked by the same nightly check.
_method: Per state and task, opened through the pipeline's HTTP client with BROWSER_HEADERS (what refresh_link_verification sends), and `_checked` records what was found. A sample ballot task is listed only where the state's voter lookup says, on its own page or in its address, that it shows a sample ballot; elsewhere the step points to the voter's county election office through USAGov's directory. A page behind a bot wall keeps its official URL, marked UNVERIFIABLE, and is never worked around (AGENTS.md section 7): its step is shown as unconfirmed, with the task's fallback beside it.
_note: A dead link on a voting step, during election week, from a link Civitas vouched for, is the worst failure this feature has. So every per-state URL is gated: a task is shown only once the liveness check (app/pipeline/fetch/ballot_lookup.py) sets `verified_at` (the page answered) or `blocked_at` (a bot wall refused the check; shown as unconfirmed, with the fallback beside it). This file never sets either. The check reads its candidate URLs from this file every run, so an edit here reaches the site on the next election run. A task unverified or missing falls back to `task_fallbacks`: NASS's Can I Vote, or USAGov's office directory for a sample ballot (vote.gov for registering, election_calendar.json's registerFallback).
